question.question: When an applied implicit-joint configuration requests automatic exit, can leadership transfer reject the last application-triggered leave proposal and then time out while the same leader remains healthy, with no implementation-owned continuation to propose exit in an otherwise idle cluster?
question.importance: A lost configuration-completion continuation can retain outgoing voters and joint quorum requirements after removal/replacement was requested, obstructing subsequent configuration changes and reducing availability. This is a scoped progress concern; no consensus-safety violation is presumed.
contexts: Same retained leader term after a bounded failed leadership transfer
Configuration genuinely committed and applied before acknowledgment
Reliable ongoing heartbeat/Ready processing after bounded transport loss, no unrelated client proposal
event_paths: ProposeConfChange -> commit -> Ready.CommittedEntries -> ApplyConfChange -> transfer begins -> Advance -> appliedTo -> MsgProp rejected
Tick -> transfer timeout -> abortLeaderTransfer -> heartbeat-only Ready/Advance

counterevidence: appliedTo retries on later applied entries; a successful transfer/new leader can append and apply a no-op.
Transfer timeout is bounded by electionTimeout and ordinary proposals are admitted after abort.

Existing TestRawNodeJointAutoLeave expects recovery after leadership loss and reelection, but does not test failed transfer with the same idle leader; parts of that test explicitly pretend a config applied, so it is not a legal-history driver to reuse unexamined.
Caller proposals may be dropped, and their retries are external. Need distinguish that from the documented AutoLeave continuation once the entering configuration was already committed/applied.

Current checker correspondence must establish that omitted diagnostics and external entropy cannot affect the repeated suffix.
question.trigger_rationale: The explicit comment at appliedTo promises retry on next advance after failed transfer, but acceptReady queues an apply response only for nonempty committed entries and abortLeaderTransfer only clears its field. Contract/source reading supplies a concrete discriminator. A controlled real-node schedule can distinguish hidden continuation from reliance on later unrelated application. This is more informative than rerunning the explained obsolete-storage-response term guard; the configuration-commit/read-release lead needs more legal-history source work before execution.

obligation.description: After a committed implicit-joint configuration has been applied and acknowledged, a retained eligible leader must preserve automatic continuation to propose leaving joint consensus when a temporary leadership-transfer blocker clears. With stable authority, available joint quorum, fair ticks, delivery and completed Ready processing, it must not enter an indefinitely repeatable idle state with AutoLeave still pending solely because no unrelated client proposal arrives.

scope.description: Implementation-owned automatic joint-exit continuation after failed leadership transfer; normal serialized RawNode Ready/Advance operation with no crashes or storage failure.
assumptions: Committed entering configuration is genuinely applied before Advance.
The same eligible leader retains authority and both constituent quorums remain available.
A bounded loss of transfer-trigger traffic is allowed; all subsequent traffic is delivered and all required Ready work completes.
No further client proposal, manual leave, forced election, restart or configuration cancellation is owed by the caller solely to implement implicit automatic exit.
excluded: No numeric completion deadline is asserted.
No claim that a finite non-completion window alone violates eventual progress.
No deployment-specific persistence failure, application business-state semantics, async-storage variant or global consensus safety verdict.

grounding.derivation: ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit promises automatic exit by proposing a zero change; Config.AutoLeave says Raft carries it out when possible. appliedTo explicitly recognizes transfer rejection and assigns retry to later advance. Once entering configuration was committed/applied, this is library continuation rather than a caller retry of an uncommitted client proposal. A closed fair suffix that keeps eligible AutoLeave pending refutes continuation without inventing a deadline.
grounding.applicability: Applied AutoLeave joint config, leader remains an incoming voter, caught-up joint voters and completed caller work; no permanent transport loss.
alternatives: Later applied client work or a new leader/no-op can provide a retry, but these are extra stimuli outside this automatic idle continuation obligation.

feedback.answered: Exploration c9ed902712d346bb8321e3b863234579 completed with exit 0. The entering config at index 5 was applied/acknowledged with node 1 leader in term 2 and transferee 2. Exactly one TimeoutNow was dropped. At tick 10 transferee cleared; through ticks 20 and 30 last/commit/applied stayed 5, AutoLeave and outgoing voters remained, while 120 further peer messages and 90 Ready batches were processed after the initial drain and application batches stayed at 9. The explicitly separate ordinary proposal then drove applied/commit to 7 and removed the outgoing set. This excludes a guaranteed retry from the exercised empty-Ready/tick suffix, but finite exploration alone is not a liveness finding.
